leftEvidence.title: A company gathers around the fugitive

points.label: Action and response
points.left: Family, distressed people, debtors, and the discontented gather to David; he places his parents in Moab before Gad directs him back to Judah.
points.right: Saul accuses his servants, Doeg reports Ahimelech, the priests are condemned, and Abiathar escapes to David, who receives responsibility for the danger.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places a hunted man becomes captain of a vulnerable company inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places the pursuit of David destroys the priestly city and binds Abiathar to him inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 1 Samuel 22:1–5 and 1 Samuel 22:6–23 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Flight, Covenant, and Restraint” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: Nob bears the cost of Saul’s suspicion

payload.tension: 1 Samuel 22:1–5 foregrounds a hunted man becomes captain of a vulnerable company; 1 Samuel 22:6–23 foregrounds the pursuit of David destroys the priestly city and binds Abiathar to him. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
